text.text: Inscription demands one tool part, three separate material offerings, and one offering of the intended stage. The part and stage offering consume one item each. The three material slots are reckoned separately and cannot answer for one another. Each must fulfil and no lower tier than the part.

The three offerings merely steady the rite. The Stigma remembers the material of the tool part itself. Manifestation takes a part native to the tool; Alienation takes one foreign to it; Sealing again takes a native part, but never the same form recorded by Manifestation.

Stigmata may deepen only in order. Choosing the next stage advances the rite; choosing the present stage rewrites that Stigma; choosing a lower stage reduces it and casts away every inscription thereafter. Advancement, rewriting, and reduction all consume the full offering. In reduction, the offered part serves the rite but leaves no record.
